items.note: Two experiments assign 139 business professionals and 319 working adults to low, moderate, or high collaboration with ChatGPT on an entrepreneurial challenge; judges, entrepreneurs, and AI rate creativity, with a curvilinear effect explained by idea diversity. The abstract says 'assigning' but not randomly; the 188-person multiwave survey is observational. Comparison is degree of AI use, check for a no-AI arm.

Two randomized controlled experiments (flash fiction writing, song composition) compare creative work with and without generative AI and test moderation by general versus domain-specific human capital. Same study as arXiv 2412.03963 ('Augmenting Minds or Automating Skills'); the abstract gives no N and does not name the output measure (search notes say rater-scored novelty and usefulness).

Classroom study of AIGC-integrated versus conventional product design ideation teaching with self-efficacy and learning outcomes; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC all empty), and a search snippet says novelty, variety, and quality of ideas were compared. Check design, N, and whether ideas were scored.

AEA RCT registration (AEARCTR-0017030, in development) that randomizes students to AI-assisted or business-as-usual research-proposal writing, with expert scores including innovativeness; planned about 400 participants. Registration only, no results; check for a later paper.

Randomized experiment with 148 three-person teams (444 people) given AI during divergent search only, convergent selection only, throughout, or never, on a product-design task; human-rated creativity and semantic exploration of proposals. Teams are the unit of assignment; PsyArXiv DOI resolves as 10.31234/osf.io/5tfng_v1.

Six-week randomized instructional experiment with 120 visual communication design undergraduates comparing GenAI-integrated with traditional instruction; blind expert ratings of creative performance were higher with GenAI. Check whether students or classes were randomized and whether AI was available when the rated work was produced.

Quasi-experiment with two 12th-grade classes (61 students) that both use ChatGPT in programming, one in individual-based and one in team-based collaboration; creativity is one of the 4Cs competencies, with no significant change. Out because the contrast is collaboration format, not AI assistance, and the creativity measure is likely a competency scale; the other screener may reasonably read it as an AI-configuration contrast.

Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment: 61 design students randomly assigned to order of traditional tools versus Midjourney/DALL-E for graphic posters; blind expert ratings of the posters were higher with AI, self-reported critical thinking lower.

University students in a digital content contest: a generative-AI (prompt literacy) group versus a conventional digital tools group, compared on creative problem-solving ability and curiosity. The abstract gives no N and does not say whether creative problem-solving was scored on the content or self-reported; may be self_report_only.

64 undergraduates in a design-thinking living lab received emotional or neutral generative-AI feedback (one AI configuration versus another); the emotional-feedback group produced higher-quality creative outputs and reported higher creative self-efficacy. Assignment method not stated.
